card.summary: The Duty Status Reform Act simplifies and consolidates the various legal authorities and categories under which members of the reserve components of the Armed Forces and the National Guard can be ordered to perform duty. It reorganizes these authorities into four distinct categories: active duty, reserve component duty, remote assignments, and specific purposes, while aligning benefits, survivor benefits, and National Guard provisions across federal law.
card.title: Duty Status Reform Act

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 6976, titled the Duty Status Reform Act, amends and reorganizes federal laws relating to duty performed by members of the reserve components of the Armed Forces, including the National Guard and the Coast Guard Reserve. The bill consolidates various authorities used to order reserve component members to perform duty into distinct categories, aligns benefits and survivor benefits across different duty statuses, repeals several older statutory sections, and updates numerous cross-references in federal law.

affected_groups.effect: Their duty statuses, mobilization authorities, training categories, and administrative procedures are reorganized and consolidated under new statutory structures.
affected_groups.group: Members of the reserve components of the Armed Forces

affected_groups.effect: National Guard duty statuses, full-time duties, training regulations, and benefit alignments are restructured within Title 32 and Title 10.
affected_groups.group: National Guard members (Army National Guard and Air National Guard)

affected_groups.effect: Applicable duty authorities and training requirements are updated to conform with the revised reserve component structure.

key_provisions: Consolidates authorities for ordering reserve component members to perform duty into chapters dividing duties into specific categories such as active duty, reserve component duty, and remote assignments.
Reorganizes and redefines provisions related to the President's authority to call the militia and National Guard into federal service, including provisions formerly known as the Insurrection Act.
Standardizes terminology across federal laws by replacing references to 'inactive-duty training' and similar terms with 'reserve component duty'.
Establishes transition provisions allowing early access to TRICARE healthcare coverage for members issued qualifying orders to active duty or full-time National Guard duty.
Sets an effective date for the consolidation provisions 10 years after enactment, while allowing for an earlier effective date if certified by relevant cabinet secretaries and enacted into law.
missing_information: Specific fiscal costs or appropriations amounts required to implement the duty status reforms.
Detailed estimates of the exact number of personnel who will immediately utilize early TRICARE access or remote assignments.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 6976, titled the Duty Status Reform Act, amends and reorganizes federal laws relating to duty performed by members of the reserve components of the Armed Forces, including the National Guard and the Coast Guard Reserve. The bill consolidates various authorities used to order reserve component members to perform duty into distinct categories, aligns benefits and survivor benefits across different duty statuses, repeals several older statutory sections, and updates numerous cross-references in federal law.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a comprehensive structural overhaul of the legal framework governing reserve component and National Guard duty in the United States. By consolidating numerous disparate authorities for ordering reservists to duty and aligning associated pay, benefits, and survivor benefits, the legislation aims to simplify military personnel administration, though its full operational implementation is slated for a 10-year timeline unless accelerated by joint departmental certification and subsequent legislation.
